title: [Rust Frontend][Perf] Use dedicated runtime for HTTP/request-processing/ZMQ
body_opening:
Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com>

## Purpose

This PR improves Rust frontend responsiveness under high-concurrency workloads with CPU-heavy request preprocessing and busy engine transport paths.

The Rust frontend now separates the main async work into dedicated runtimes:

- HTTP runtime: accepts connections, routes lightweight endpoints, and writes responses.
- Request runtime: runs heavyweight inference/tokenization endpoints through Axum middleware, covering request extraction, validation, chat-template rendering, tokenization, request lowering, and engine submission.
- ZMQ runtime: drives engine-core transport send/receive, output dispatch, abort handling, and coordinator task

title: fix(dsv4): correct software FP8 RNE encoding and edge cases
body_opening:
## Problem

The software float -> FP8 E4M3 cast saturates far too early.

```c
exp8 = exp32 + kBias;
...
if (exp8 >= kMaxExp) return sign | kSaturate;
```

With `kMaxExp = 15`, that fires at `|val| >= 128` for FNUZ (bias 8) and `|val| >= 256` for FN
(bias 7) — while `fp8_e4m3_clip` admits up to **224** and **448** respectively.

| flavour | collapsed range | encoded as | error at the low end |
|---|---|---|---|
| E4M3FNUZ (gfx942) | `[128, 224]` | `0x7F` = 240 | **87.5%** |
| E4M3FN | `[256, 448]` | 448 | **75%** |

This is not a rare corner. `cast_to_ue8m0` rounds the group exponent **up**, so the affected
band is exactly where the *largest* element of each 64-value quantization group lands

Adds an SM120 (consumer Blackwell, e.g. RTX 5090) dense BF16 decode GEMM and skinny GEMV, registered per the KDA kernel format (`KernelBackend.KDA`), plus two engine fixes. Together these bring **gemma-4-E2B-it** decode to parity with vLLM at bs=1 and bs=16 on a single RTX 5090.

title: [HiCache] Optimize L2 mem allocation when cache miss in L3

When enabling HiCache, every L1 hit will trigger a write from L1 -> L2 -> L3, which leads to the L2 memory full at all times.
